scoring_note: Candidate-only, non-authorizing. Prophecy scores low across these letters by the rubric's own terms; the other four criteria were scored on argument structure, embedded traditions, text-critical and syntactic cruxes, cross-book parallels, and reception facts. Ecclesial disagreement and authorship/composite questions are reported as neutral facts of reception, never adjudicated. Where calibration was uncertain the score was set upward.

evidence.translation_difficulty: Text-critical cruxes sit at boundary-relevant points: 14:34-35 (transposed after 14:40 in D F G and Latin witnesses; interpolation hypothesis), 13:3 kauchesomai/kauthesomai (boast/be burned), 15:51 (three variant forms of 'we shall not all sleep'), 2:1 mysterion/martyrion, 11:24 'broken'. Lexical cruxes: 6:9 malakoi/arsenokoitai (arsenokoites first attested here), 7:36-38 parthenos and hyperakmos (daughter vs fiancee), 11:10 exousia 'on the head', 15:29 baptism 'for' the dead, 16:22 Aramaic maranatha. Unmarked Corinthian slogans (6:12, 6:13, 7:1, 8:1, 8:4, 8:8, 10:23) require the translator to decide where quotation ends and refutation begins.
evidence.literature_type_difficulty: The most generically mixed Pauline letter: peri de topical headings (7:1, 7:25, 8:1, 12:1, 16:1, 16:12); slogan-and-refutation diatribe (6:12-20, 10:23); halakhic-style rulings on marriage (ch 7); Exodus typology/midrash (10:1-13); liturgical tradition (11:23-26); the love encomium (ch 13) inset between two gift discussions; a creedal tradition (15:3-7); apocalyptic disclosure (15:51-52); vice lists (5:10-11, 6:9-10); collection and travel notes (16:1-12).
evidence.prophecy: Chapter 15 is a sustained eschatological argument whose sub-seams (15:20, 15:29, 15:35, 15:50/51) rest on argument logic; 15:23-28 is a predictive sequence (then... then the end) and 15:51-57 a 'mystery' disclosure. Shorter eschatological signals: 3:13-15 the Day, 4:5, 6:2-3, 7:29-31, 13:8-12 'when the perfect comes'. Chapters 12-14 discuss prophecy as a gift rather than delivering it.
evidence.connections: About seventeen explicit OT citations: 1:19 Isa 29:14; 1:31 Jer 9:24; 2:9 composite Isa 64:4; 2:16 Isa 40:13; 3:19-20 Job 5:13 + Ps 94:11; 5:13 Deut 17:7; 6:16 Gen 2:24; 9:9 Deut 25:4; 10:7 Exod 32:6; 10:26 Ps 24:1; 14:21 Isa 28:11-12; 15:27 Ps 8:6; 15:32 Isa 22:13; 15:45 Gen 2:7; 15:54-55 Isa 25:8 + Hos 13:14. Jesus tradition cited as ruling (7:10-11, 9:14, 11:23-25 parallel Luke 22:19-20); Adam-Christ typology shared with Rom 5; weak/strong argument parallel to Rom 14-15; collection parallel to 2 Cor 8-9 and Rom 15:25-28; Acts 18 setting.
evidence.ecclesial_contestedness: Reception fact, not adjudicated: 11:23-34 Eucharist ('this is my body', discerning the body, unworthy reception) read differently across Catholic, Orthodox, Lutheran, Reformed and memorialist traditions; 11:2-16 head coverings and kephale (source vs authority) and 14:34-35 women's silence bear on ordination debates and carry an interpolation question; 3:10-15 'saved as through fire' figures in purgatory discussions; 7:10-16 divorce/remarriage and the 'Pauline privilege' (Catholic canon law vs Orthodox economia vs Protestant practice); 12-14 tongues and prophecy (cessationist vs continuationist); 13:8-12 'the perfect'; 15:29 baptism for the dead (LDS practice vs mainstream readings); 6:9-11 contemporary ethics debates; 5:1-13 discipline.

books.boundary_risk: The peri de headings are real text signals but the arguments outrun chapter divisions: 8:1-11:1 is one idol-food argument with ch 9 as an embedded self-example (a seam at 9:1 or 10:1 severs it), 12-14 is one argument with ch 13 inset, 15 is one argument, and 1:10-4:21 one section on divisions. Slogan-refutation pairs (6:12-13, 10:23) and tradition-plus-application blocks (11:23-26 with 11:27-34; 15:3-7 with 15:8-11) must not be split at the quotation edge.
extra_scrutiny_focus: 8:1-11:1 idol-food argument with the ch 9 digression
12:1-14:40 with ch 13 inset and 14:33b-36 text-critical block
books.uncertainty: WEB NT follows the Greek Majority Text (from memory of the WEB preface, not verified here), so it will carry Byzantine readings at 13:3, 15:51 and elsewhere; whether WEB marks the Corinthian slogans with quotation marks is unverified. The Greek substrate the campaign will stage for the NT is unknown to this scorer.

evidence.translation_difficulty: Widely rated the hardest Greek in the Pauline corpus: long anacoluthic periods in 1:12-2:4 and 3:1-4:6, the yes/no wordplay of 1:15-22, 2:14 thriambeuo (led in triumph as captive vs caused to triumph), 3:17 'the Lord is the Spirit', 5:1-10 tent/clothing/naked metaphors with ekdemeo/endemeo, 5:21 'made him sin', 12:7 skolops and the dio variant. 6:14-7:1 packs six NT hapax legomena into eight verses (heterozygeo, metoche, symphonesis, Beliar, synkatathesis, molysmos); 8:20 hadrotes is hapax. Verse numbering differs across traditions at the close: 13:12-14 (KJV/WEB) vs 13:12-13 (NA28/Vulgate). Variants at 1:10, 3:2 hymon/hemon, 8:7.
evidence.literature_type_difficulty: Apologetic self-defense with an interrupted travelogue (2:12-13 resumed at 7:5), a theological excursus on Exod 34 (3:7-18), three peristasis catalogues (4:8-9, 6:4-10, 11:23-29), an OT catena (6:16-18), two fund-raising appeals (chs 8 and 9), the ironic 'fool's speech' (11:1-12:13) containing a heavenly-ascent report (12:1-10), and third-visit warnings (12:14-13:10). Register shifts (irony, parody of boasting) are themselves unit markers.
evidence.prophecy: Low: 5:10 judgment seat and 4:14 resurrection are passing; 12:1-4 is a vision report, not prediction; 5:1-10 is eschatological argument. Not a boundary driver.
evidence.connections: 3:7-18 reworks Exod 34:29-35; the 6:16-18 catena joins Lev 26:12, Ezek 37:27, Isa 52:11, 2 Sam 7:14, Isa 43:6; further citations at 4:13 Ps 116:10, 6:2 Isa 49:8, 8:15 Exod 16:18, 9:9 Ps 112:9, 9:10 Isa 55:10 + Hos 10:12, 10:17 Jer 9:24 (shared with 1 Cor 1:31), 13:1 Deut 19:15. Cross-book dependencies: the offender of 2:5-11 and the 'painful letter' (2:3-4, 7:8) relate to 1 Cor; the collection to 1 Cor 16 and Rom 15; 11:32-33 parallels Acts 9:23-25; 11:24-25 hardships absent from Acts.
evidence.ecclesial_contestedness: Composite-construction question (reception fact, not adjudicated): partition hypotheses treat chs 10-13 as the severe letter or a later letter, 6:14-7:1 as a non-Pauline insertion, chs 8 and 9 as two collection notes, and 2:14-7:4 as separate; the seams at 2:13/2:14, 6:13/6:14, 7:1/7:2, 7:4/7:5, 9:15/10:1 are exactly where these hypotheses cut. Doctrinal reception: 5:21 imputation vs participation (Reformation vs Catholic/Orthodox readings), 5:1-10 and 5:8 intermediate state, 3:6 letter/spirit hermeneutics, 3:17 pneumatology, 6:14 'unequally yoked' in marriage practice, 12:7 the thorn's identity, 13:14 trinitarian benediction in liturgy.

books.boundary_risk: A chunker following topic or chapter can sever the 2:14-7:4 excursus from its travel frame (2:12-13 / 7:5-16) or fail to mark the resumption at 7:5; 6:14-7:1 reads as a self-contained block whose edges look like textual joins; 9:1 restarts the collection appeal after ch 8; 10:1 is an abrupt tonal break; the fool's speech must be held as one ironic unit across its relaunch at 11:16-21a, the vision at 12:1 and the close at 12:11-13.
extra_scrutiny_focus: 2:12-13 and 7:5-16 travel frame around the 2:14-7:4 excursus
3:7-18 Exod 34 midrash and 3:1-6 letters of recommendation
10:1 tonal break and 10:1-18 boundaries of boasting
12:14-13:10 third-visit warnings and 13:11-14 close with the numbering difference
books.uncertainty: The 13:12-14 vs 13:12-13 numbering claim is from memory of KJV/NA28 practice and should be checked against the staged WEB verse map; WEB Majority-Text basis not verified here.

evidence.translation_difficulty: 2:16, 2:20, 3:22 pistis Christou (objective vs subjective genitive) changes the rendering of the thesis; 3:19-20 ('ordained through angels by a mediator; a mediator is not of one') is famously obscure; 3:16 sperma singular argument; 4:3, 4:9 stoicheia (elements vs elemental spirits); 3:24 paidagogos; 4:12-20 allusive situation (4:13 di' astheneian); 5:12 apokopsontai (castrate) euphemism handling; 6:16 'and upon the Israel of God' (kai epexegetical or additive). Text: 1:18 Kephas/Petros, 2:5 hois oude omitted in Western witnesses, 3:1 Byzantine addition 'that you should not obey the truth', 4:25 to de Hagar Sina / to gar Sina. The extent of Paul's speech to Peter (ends at 2:14 or runs to 2:21) is unmarked in Greek and is a translator's decision.
evidence.literature_type_difficulty: Apologetic letter with no thanksgiving (1:6 astonishment opening); autobiographical narratio (1:11-2:14) containing a speech of unmarked extent (2:14-21); scriptural argument on Abraham (3:6-29) with a legal illustration (3:15-18); personal appeal (4:12-20) interrupting the argument; the Hagar/Sarah allegory (4:21-31); paraenesis with vice/virtue catalogues (5:19-23); an autograph postscript (6:11-18). Rhetorical-genre classification (forensic vs deliberative) is itself disputed.
evidence.prophecy: Present but not a boundary driver: oracular quotations embedded in argument (3:11 Hab 2:4; 4:27 Isa 54:1), Scripture 'foreseeing' (3:8), eschatological warning and harvest (5:5, 5:21, 6:7-9).
evidence.connections: 3:6-14 chains six citations in nine verses (Gen 15:6; Gen 12:3/18:18; Deut 27:26; Hab 2:4; Lev 18:5; Deut 21:23), then 3:16 Gen 13:15/17:8, 4:27 Isa 54:1, 4:30 Gen 21:10, 5:14 Lev 19:18, over the Gen 16-21 Hagar/Sarah narrative. Cross-book dependencies: the Jerusalem visits 1:18 and 2:1-10 against Acts 9, 11, 15 (a classic chronology problem) and the Antioch incident 2:11-14; Rom 4 (Abraham), Rom 1:17 (Hab 2:4), Rom 7-8 (flesh/Spirit), Rom 13:8-10 (love fulfils law); 3:28 with 1 Cor 12:13 and Col 3:11.
evidence.ecclesial_contestedness: Reception fact, not adjudicated: 2:16 and 3:10-14 justification by faith and 'works of the law' are read differently by Reformation, Catholic (Trent), Orthodox and New Perspective interpreters; 5:6 'faith working through love' and 5:4 'fallen from grace' figure in Trent/Reformed and perseverance debates; 2:11-14 Peter/Paul confrontation has a long reception history (Jerome-Augustine correspondence; papal-authority discussions); 3:28 in gender and ordination debates; 4:21-31 allegory in hermeneutics and Church-Israel questions; 6:16 identity of 'the Israel of God'; 3:19-25 the purpose of the law.

books.boundary_risk: The end of the reported speech at 2:14 is unmarked, so a seam at 2:15 or 2:17 severs the speech from the thesis it becomes; 4:8-20 interrupts the scriptural argument, which resumes at 4:21, so the allegory can be stranded; 5:1 is a hinge (close of the allegory or opening of the exhortation) that WEB paragraphing may decide but E-23 bars as evidence; 5:13 and 6:1 paraenesis seams are weakly marked.
books.uncertainty: Whether WEB carries the Byzantine 3:1 addition and the 4:25 reading is unverified here.

evidence.translation_difficulty: 1:1 'in Ephesus' is absent from P46, Sinaiticus and Vaticanus (circular-letter and Marcion 'Laodiceans' questions) - the address itself is text-critically open. Syntax: 1:3-14 is one Greek sentence (about 200 words), 1:15-23 another, 2:1-7 an anacoluthon whose 'you' (2:1) is resumed at 2:5, and 3:1 breaks off to be resumed at 3:14; every translation-created sentence break inside these is a potential false seam. 4:8 cites Ps 68:18 with 'gave' for 'received'; 4:9 'the lower parts of the earth' (partitive vs appositive) and the added 'first' variant; 5:21-22 the verb of 5:22 is supplied from 5:21 in the best witnesses (B, P46 lack it), so the hinge between the participle chain and the household code is unstable; 1:23 pleroumenou middle/passive; 1:10 anakephalaiosasthai; 2:20 akrogoniaios cornerstone/capstone.
evidence.literature_type_difficulty: Berakah/eulogy (1:3-14), two intercessory prayer-reports (1:15-23; 3:14-21) with a doxology (3:20-21), a mystery-disclosure digression (3:2-13), a possible hymnic piece (2:14-16), a creedal acclamation (4:4-6), a quoted hymn fragment introduced as 'it says' (5:14), catalogue paraenesis (4:17-5:20), a Haustafel (5:21-6:9) and the armor allegory (6:10-20).
evidence.prophecy: Low: 1:9-10 summing up in the fullness of times, 5:5 inheritance warning, 6:12-13 'the evil day', 5:14 oracle-like citation. Not a boundary driver.
evidence.connections: Shares roughly a third of its material with Colossians, some of it near-verbatim (6:21-22 // Col 4:7-8 Tychicus note; 5:22-6:9 // Col 3:18-4:1; 4:22-32 // Col 3:5-12; 5:19-20 // Col 3:16-17; 2:5 // Col 2:13; 4:16 // Col 2:19), so row seams should be checked against Colossians. OT: 1:22 Ps 8:6; 2:17 Isa 57:19 + 52:7; 2:20 Isa 28:16; 4:8 Ps 68:18; 4:25 Zech 8:16; 4:26 Ps 4:4; 5:18 Prov 23:31 LXX; 5:31 Gen 2:24; 6:2-3 Exod 20:12/Deut 5:16; 6:14-17 armor from Isa 11:5, 59:17, 52:7, 49:2 (and Wis 5:17-20); 5:14 possibly Isa 60:1/26:19. Household-code parallels with 1 Pet 2:18-3:7.
evidence.ecclesial_contestedness: Reception fact, not adjudicated: authorship (Pauline vs deutero-Pauline) is disputed; 1:4-5, 11 election/predestination (Reformed vs Arminian, Catholic, Orthodox readings); 2:8-10 grace, faith and works; 4:5 'one baptism'; 4:8-10 the descent (Apostles' Creed descensus, harrowing of hell vs descent-to-earth readings); 4:11 fivefold ministry (charismatic vs cessationist; polity); 5:21-33 headship/submission and 5:32 mysterion rendered sacramentum (cited at Trent on matrimony) vs non-sacramental readings; 6:5-9 slavery in reception history.

books.boundary_risk: Translation-created breaks inside 1:3-14 and 1:15-23 can be mistaken for unit seams; 3:14-21 must not be detached from the prayer begun at 3:1 across the 3:2-13 digression; 5:21 is a hinge whose assignment (end of 5:18-21 or head of the household code) is syntactically and text-critically contested; 4:1 is a strong indicative/imperative turn but 4:17, 5:1-2, 5:15 and 6:10 are weaker internal seams; the 4:4-6 acclamation and 5:14 fragment must stay with their frames.
books.uncertainty: WEB (Majority Text) will read 'in Ephesus' at 1:1 and supply a verb at 5:22; not byte-verified here.

evidence.translation_difficulty: The Christ hymn carries the letter's cruxes: 2:6 harpagmos (NT hapax; 'a thing to be grasped' vs 'exploited', res rapta vs res rapienda), morphe theou, 2:7 ekenosen 'emptied himself'. Elsewhere: 1:7 hymas/hemas ('you have me in your heart' or 'I have you'); 2:1 ei tis splanchna solecism; 4:3 gnesie syzyge (yokefellow or a proper name Syzygus); 4:18 apecho commercial idiom; 3:2 katatome/peritome pun; 1:1 episkopois kai diakonois office rendering; 3:20 politeuma. Text: Byzantine longer readings at 3:16 ('let us walk by the same rule, let us mind the same thing') and 4:13 ('through Christ'), 1:14 'of God' addition, 3:3 theou/theo.
evidence.literature_type_difficulty: Friendship/family letter containing a strophic hymn whose stanza division (two, three or six) and edges (does it begin at 2:5 or 2:6; are 2:8c 'even death of the cross' and 2:11c Pauline additions) are contested; travel plans and commendations (2:19-30); abrupt polemic and autobiography (3:2-21); paraenesis (4:2-9); a thank-you note in commercial idiom (4:10-20). Two 'finally' closures (3:1, 4:8) inside the letter.
evidence.prophecy: Low: 3:20-21 transformation of the body, the 'day of Christ' motif (1:6, 1:10, 2:16), 2:10-11 future universal confession citing Isa 45:23, 4:5 'the Lord is near'.
evidence.connections: Quotations without formula: 2:10-11 Isa 45:23; 1:19 Job 13:16 LXX verbatim ('this will turn out to my deliverance'); 2:15 Deut 32:5 ('crooked and perverse generation'); 2:14 Exod 16 murmuring; 4:3 Ps 69:28 book of life. Contested echoes of Isa 53 and of Gen 2-3 (Adam) in 2:6-8. Cross-book: Acts 16:11-40 founding (Lydia, the jailer); 3:9 with Rom 3:21-22 and Gal 2:16; 2 Cor 8:1-5 Macedonian giving; imprisonment provenance shared with Col/Phlm (Rome, Ephesus or Caesarea disputed).
evidence.ecclesial_contestedness: Reception fact, not adjudicated: 2:6-11 kenosis christology (kenotic theories vs Chalcedonian readings; harpagmos); 2:12-13 'work out your salvation... God works in you' (synergism vs monergism across Orthodox, Catholic, Lutheran and Reformed readings); 1:1 bishops and deacons in polity debates (monepiscopacy vs presbyterian identity of offices); 1:23 'depart and be with Christ' in intermediate-state and soul-sleep discussions; 3:12-16 in perfectionism traditions; 2:10 'every knee' in universalism debates; partition hypotheses (three-letter theories cutting at 3:1/3:2 and 4:10-20; Polycarp's plural 'letters') are a composition-reception fact.

books.boundary_risk: 3:1 'finally, rejoice' followed by the 3:2 polemic invites a false major seam; the hymn is cited as an argument, so 2:1-5 and 2:12-18 must not be severed from 2:6-11; 4:10-20 versus 4:2-9 and the second 'finally' at 4:8; 1:27-2:4 runs into the hymn without a sentence break at 2:5.
books.uncertainty: WEB readings at 3:16 and 4:13 (Byzantine longer forms) not byte-verified here; the Isa 53 and Adam echoes in 2:6-8 are contested in scholarship and are listed as candidates only.

evidence.translation_difficulty: Difficulty concentrates in 2:8-23: stoicheia tou kosmou (2:8, 2:20); 2:18 thelon en tapeinophrosyne, threskeia ton angelon (worship of/by angels), embateuon (hapax; mystery-initiation term) and the ha heoraken variant with or without 'not'; 2:23 ethelothreskia (hapax) and 'not of any value against the indulgence of the flesh', one of the NT's most obscure sentences; 2:14 cheirographon tois dogmasin (hapax); 2:15 apekdysamenos middle voice (who is stripped). Also 1:24 antanaplero (hapax) 'what is lacking of the afflictions of Christ'; 1:15 prototokos pases ktiseos (of/over creation); 2:2 'the mystery of God' with multiple variant expansions (Byzantine 'of God, both of the Father and of Christ'); 1:14 Byzantine 'through his blood'; 3:6 'on the sons of disobedience' omitted in some witnesses; 1:7, 1:12 hymon/hemon.
evidence.literature_type_difficulty: Thanksgiving-prayer (1:3-14) leading into the Christ hymn (1:15-20; strophic division and possible additions 'the church' 1:18, 'through the blood of his cross' 1:20 contested), apostolic self-presentation (1:24-2:5), polemic against the 'philosophy' (2:8-23), baptismal catechesis with vice/virtue lists (3:1-17), a Haustafel (3:18-4:1), and greetings with commendations and a letter-exchange instruction (4:7-18).
evidence.prophecy: Low: 3:4 'when Christ is revealed', 2:17 'shadow of things to come', 1:5 hope laid up in heaven. Not a boundary driver.
evidence.connections: Ephesians parallels at row level (3:18-4:1 // Eph 5:22-6:9; 4:7-8 // Eph 6:21-22 near-verbatim; 3:5-12 // Eph 4:22-32; 3:16-17 // Eph 5:19-20; 2:13 // Eph 2:5; 2:19 // Eph 4:16) and Philemon name overlap (4:9 Onesimus; 4:10 Aristarchus, Mark; 4:12 Epaphras; 4:14 Luke, Demas; 4:17 Archippus // Phlm 1-2, 10, 23-24). OT and wisdom: 1:15-17 Gen 1 with Prov 8:22 and Wis 7:26 wisdom christology; 2:22 Isa 29:13 (as in Mark 7:7); 3:1 Ps 110:1; 3:10 Gen 1:26-27; 2:11 Gen 17 circumcision; 2:3 Isa 45:3/Prov 2:3-4. 4:16 references a Laodicean letter (apocryphal Epistle to the Laodiceans in reception).
evidence.ecclesial_contestedness: Reception fact, not adjudicated: authorship disputed; 1:15-17 prototokos in Arian controversy and in Jehovah's Witness rendering ('all [other] things'); 1:24 'what is lacking in Christ's afflictions' read within Catholic teaching on redemptive suffering and read otherwise by Protestant interpreters; 2:11-12 baptism-as-circumcision used in paedobaptist argument and contested by credobaptists; 2:16-17 Sabbath and festivals (Seventh-day Adventist vs mainstream readings); 2:18 'worship of angels' and 2:20-23 asceticism in Reformation-era polemic; 3:18-4:1 household code; 4:16 the missing letter.

books.boundary_risk: The hymn 1:15-20 is bound to its frame (1:12-14 relative clause 'in whom'; 1:21-23 application), so a seam at 1:15 or 1:21 must be argued not assumed; 2:6-7 is the hinge between exposition and polemic and 2:8-23 must be held as one polemic despite its 2:16, 2:18, 2:20 sub-starts; 3:1-4 grounds the paraenesis and belongs with neither chapter division cleanly; 4:2-6 and 4:7-18 are short, over-split-prone closers.
extra_scrutiny_focus: 4:7-18 greetings aligned with Phlm and Eph 6:21-22
books.uncertainty: WEB Majority readings at 1:14, 2:2, 2:18, 3:6 not byte-verified here.

evidence.translation_difficulty: Plain Koine with a few real cruxes: 2:7 nepioi/epioi ('infants'/'gentle', one-letter variant split between NA28 and the Byzantine text); 4:4 skeuos (wife or body) with ktasthai (acquire or control); 2:16 eis telos ('at last', 'completely'); 4:17 harpagesometha and apantesis (civic-reception term); 5:23 spirit-soul-body; 3:3 sainesthai (hapax); 4:6 en to pragmati. The verse division 2:6/2:7 differs between KJV/WEB and NA28 ('as apostles of Christ' assigned to 2:6 or 2:7). Byzantine expansions at 1:1 ('from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ') and 3:2 diakonon.
evidence.literature_type_difficulty: An extended thanksgiving that arguably runs 1:2-3:13, so the body's onset (2:1, 2:17 or 4:1) is a judgment call; apostolic self-defense narratio (2:1-12); a polemical excursus (2:13-16, subject of an interpolation hypothesis); apostolic-parousia travelogue (2:17-3:10); wish-prayers (3:11-13; 5:23-24); paraenesis with peri de headings (4:9, 5:1); apocalyptic instruction (4:13-18; 5:1-11) citing a 'word of the Lord' (4:15); a staccato run of imperatives (5:12-22).
evidence.prophecy: Substantial: 4:13-18 (the descent, the archangel, the catching up) and 5:1-11 (day of the Lord, thief, birth pangs) are the letter's center and their seam at 5:1 (peri de) is a judgment call; every chapter closes on the parousia (1:10; 2:19-20; 3:13; 5:23), making eschatological closure a structural device that boundaries must weigh from both sides.
evidence.connections: 2 Thessalonians parallels (1:1 // 2 Thess 1:1-2; 2:9 // 2 Thess 3:8 verbatim 'labor and toil, night and day'; 3:11-13 // 2 Thess 2:16-17; 5:1-2 against 2 Thess 2:1-2) and the dependence question; Acts 17:1-10 founding and 18:5 Timothy's arrival (3:6); Jesus tradition (4:15 'word of the Lord'; 5:2 thief as Matt 24:43/Luke 12:39; 5:3 birth pangs as Mark 13:8; 4:16-17 with Matt 24:30-31); OT: 2:16 Gen 15:16 'fill up sins', 4:5 Ps 79:6/Jer 10:25, 4:8 Ezek 36:27/37:14, 5:8 Isa 59:17 armor (shared with Eph 6:14-17), 5:22 Job 1:1 LXX; 5:15 with Rom 12:17.
evidence.ecclesial_contestedness: Reception fact, not adjudicated: 4:13-18 is the foundational 'rapture' text and is read on pre-tribulation, mid, post and non-dispensational schemes; 2:14-16 ('the Jews... wrath has come upon them') in Jewish-Christian relations and the interpolation hypothesis; 4:13-14 'sleep' in soul-sleep (Adventist, Jehovah's Witness) vs conscious-intermediate-state readings; 5:23 trichotomy vs dichotomy; 5:19-21 prophecy in charismatic reception; 4:4 vessel in marriage ethics.

books.boundary_risk: The thanksgiving-body seam is unmarked (2:1, 2:17, 4:1 all defensible); 2:13-16 sits as a second thanksgiving and can be stranded or absorbed; 4:13-18 and 5:1-11 must be split only on the peri de of 5:1 with the eschatological unity disclosed; 5:12-22 is easily over-split; the chapter-closing parousia formulae are closures and a seam beside them must be weighed from both sides.
extra_scrutiny_focus: 4:13-5:11 split at 5:1 and the 4:15 citation extent
2:6/2:7 numbering and the 2:7 variant in WEB
books.uncertainty: The 2:6/2:7 division difference and WEB's 'gentle' at 2:7 are from memory of KJV/NA28 practice, not byte-verified here.

evidence.translation_difficulty: Cruxes cluster in ch 2, the book's core: 2:2 enesteken ('has come' vs 'is at hand'); 2:6-7 to katechon / ho katechon ('what/who restrains'), notoriously obscure; 2:3 anomias/hamartias ('man of lawlessness'/'man of sin', the Byzantine reading); 2:13 aparchen/ap' arches ('as firstfruits'/'from the beginning', Byzantine); 2:8 'Lord Jesus' with Iesous omitted in some witnesses; 2:11 energeian planes. 1:3-10 is a single Greek sentence in which thanksgiving turns into judgment theophany. 3:6 variant forms of 'received'; 3:11 ergazomenous/periergazomenous wordplay; 1:9 olethron aionion.
evidence.literature_type_difficulty: Thanksgiving fused with a judgment theophany in OT diction (1:3-12, possibly incorporating traditional material); a mini-apocalypse (2:1-12: apostasy, man of lawlessness, restrainer, parousia of the lawless one, mystery of lawlessness) with an aside (2:5); a second thanksgiving (2:13-14); tradition-appeal (2:15); wish-prayers (2:16-17; 3:5; 3:16); a command on the disorderly with an example-narrative inset (3:6-15, 3:7-9); autograph authentication (3:17).
evidence.prophecy: A principal driver: 2:1-12 is predictive apocalyptic whose sub-seams (2:3-4 the sign; 2:5 aside; 2:6-7 restrainer; 2:8-10 parousia and destruction; 2:11-12 delusion) rest on interpretive judgment; 1:5-10 depicts the revelation of the Lord in flaming fire; 2:13 returns to thanksgiving as a real seam.
evidence.connections: 1:5-12 is an Isaiah mosaic (1:8 Isa 66:15 + Ps 79:6/Jer 10:25; 1:9 Isa 2:10, 19, 21 near-verbatim LXX; 1:10 Ps 89:7 LXX + Ps 68:35; 1:12 Isa 66:5); 2:4 draws on Dan 11:36 and Ezek 28:2 with the abomination of Dan 9:27/11:31; 2:8 Isa 11:4; 2:13 Deut 33:12; the Synoptic apocalypse (deception Mark 13:5, abomination 13:14, false signs 13:22 // Matt 24:4-5, 24) and later parallels in 1 John 2:18 and Rev 13; 1 Thessalonians parallels throughout (1:1-2; 3:8 // 1 Thess 2:9; 2:1-2 against 1 Thess 5:1-2) and 3:17 'in every letter'.
evidence.ecclesial_contestedness: Reception fact, not adjudicated: 2:3-12 identifications of the man of lawlessness and the restrainer differ across traditions (Reformation-era confessions such as the Westminster Confession 25.6 original text and the Smalcald Articles identify the papacy; Catholic teaching in the Catechism 675-677 speaks of a final trial and the Antichrist's deception; futurist, historicist and preterist schemes coexist); 2:15 'hold the traditions... by word or by letter' is cited in Catholic/Orthodox accounts of Tradition and read otherwise under sola scriptura; 2:11 God sending delusion (reprobation); 1:9 'eternal destruction' in annihilationism vs eternal-punishment debates; 3:6-15 discipline and 3:10 in social ethics; authorship disputed.

books.boundary_risk: A seam at 1:5 or 1:6 inside the single sentence 1:3-10 is translation-created; 2:1-12 must be held as one argument with its steps disclosed, and 2:13 marked as the real return to thanksgiving; 2:15-17 close ch 2 and 3:1-5 transition to the disorderly command, whose 3:7-9 example inset invites over-splitting; the 3:17 autograph is a closure device.
books.uncertainty: WEB readings at 2:3 ('man of sin') and 2:13 ('from the beginning') are inferred from the Majority-Text basis, not byte-verified here.

evidence.translation_difficulty: 3:16 hos/theos ('who was manifested' vs 'God was manifested', the Byzantine reading) is the letter's famous variant; 2:15 'saved through the childbearing' is its hardest sentence; 2:12 authentein (NT hapax: have authority / assume authority / domineer); 3:2, 3:12 and 5:9 'one-woman man' / 'one-man woman' idiom; 5:16 pistos e piste (Byzantine 'believing man or woman' vs 'believing woman'); 6:5 Byzantine addition 'withdraw yourself from such'; 4:10 'Savior of all men, especially of believers'; 1:9-10 vice list with arsenokoitais; 1:4 genealogies; 6:10 'a root of all kinds of evil'. The pistos ho logos formula's direction (1:15 forward; 3:1a backward to 2:15 or forward to 3:1b; 4:9 backward to 4:8 or forward to 4:10) is a syntax decision that fixes seams.
evidence.literature_type_difficulty: Church-order/mandate letter with a loose structure: a charge (1:3-7) resumed at 1:18 after two digressions (1:8-11 law; 1:12-17 autobiographical thanksgiving with doxology 1:17); prayer instruction (2:1-7); women (2:8-15); office qualification lists (3:1-13); a six-line hymn/creed (3:16); prophetic warning (4:1-5); three 'faithful sayings' (1:15; 3:1; 4:9); quasi-legal widow enrolment rules (5:3-16); elder discipline (5:17-25) with the 5:23 personal aside; slaves (6:1-2); polemic (6:3-10; 6:20-21); a solemn charge with doxology (6:11-16); riches (6:17-19).
evidence.prophecy: Low: 4:1-5 'the Spirit says expressly' about later times; 1:18 and 4:14 prophecies over Timothy; 6:14-15 the appearing. Not a boundary driver beyond marking 4:1-5 as a unit.
evidence.connections: Pastoral parallels (Titus 1:5-9 // 3:1-7 qualifications; 2 Tim 2:22-26 // 6:11; Titus 3:9 // 1:4; Hymenaeus 1:20 // 2 Tim 2:17; Alexander 1:20 // 2 Tim 4:14); 5:18 cites Deut 25:4 (as 1 Cor 9:9) together with a Jesus saying (Luke 10:7) as 'scripture'; 5:19 Deut 19:15 (as 2 Cor 13:1; Matt 18:16); 2:13-14 Gen 2-3 (as 1 Cor 11:8-9; 2 Cor 11:3); 6:7 Job 1:21/Eccl 5:15; 6:16 Exod 33:20; 1:17 doxology with Tob 13:7, 11 diction; 2:5-6 with Mark 10:45; 6:13 Pilate with John 18:37; 1:12-16 with Acts 8-9; 1:3 Ephesus with Acts 20; 3:16 with the Phil 2 and Col 1 hymns.
evidence.ecclesial_contestedness: Reception fact, not adjudicated: 2:8-15 women's teaching and 2:15 childbearing (complementarian vs egalitarian; Catholic and Orthodox arguments on ordination); 3:1-13 offices ('husband of one wife' in clerical celibacy and remarriage rules; 3:11 women deacons; monepiscopacy); 3:15 church as 'pillar and ground of the truth' in Catholic/Orthodox ecclesiology vs sola scriptura; 2:4 God 'desires all people to be saved' (Calvinist vs Arminian and Catholic readings); 4:1-5 forbidding marriage and foods (Reformation-era polemic, e.g. Apology of the Augsburg Confession XXIII, vs Catholic readings); 5:3-16 order of widows; 5:17 paid ministry; 4:14 and 5:22 laying on of hands and succession; 3:16 variant in Byzantine-priority debates; authorship of the Pastorals disputed.

books.boundary_risk: The faithful-saying formulas decide whether 2:15 and 3:1 share a row and whether 4:8 and 4:10 do; 1:3-20 is one charge split by two digressions and a chunker may treat 1:12-17 as free-standing; 6:2b-10 and 6:17-19 (riches) bracket the 6:11-16 charge, so a topical chunker may wrongly reunite them or split the charge; 3:14-16 (purpose statement plus hymn) is a hinge unit; 5:23 is an aside inside 5:17-25.
extra_scrutiny_focus: 5:3-16 widows and 5:17-25 elders with the 5:23 aside
books.uncertainty: WEB readings at 3:16 ('God'), 5:16 and 6:5 are inferred from the Majority-Text basis, not byte-verified here.

evidence.translation_difficulty: 3:16 pasa graphe theopneustos (predicate 'all scripture is God-breathed and profitable' vs attributive 'every God-breathed scripture is also profitable'); 2:11a 'faithful is the saying' pointing backward to 2:8-10 or forward to the 2:11b-13 hymn; 1:12 paratheke ('what I have committed to him' or 'what has been committed to me'); 2:26 autou/ekeinou with three possible referents; 4:13 phailones and membranas (hapax: cloak, parchments); 3:6 gynaikaria (hapax); 2:19 an OT-like second line of uncertain source. Byzantine readings at 1:11 ('of the Gentiles'), 2:14 kyriou/theou, 4:22 longer benediction; 4:10 Galatia/Gallia.
evidence.literature_type_difficulty: Testament/farewell paraenesis (4:6-8 'I have fought the good fight') with thanksgiving (1:3-5), charge (1:6-14; 2:1-7 with soldier, athlete, farmer metaphors), a creedal summary (2:8), a four-line conditional hymn (2:11-13), polemic (2:14-26; 3:1-9 last-days vice list with the extra-biblical Jannes and Jambres), autobiographical example (3:10-13), the Scripture statement (3:14-17), solemn charge (4:1-5), and dense personalia (4:9-22: Demas, Crescens, Luke, Mark, Tychicus, the cloak and books, Alexander, the first defense).
evidence.prophecy: Low: 3:1-9 'in the last days' and 4:3-4 'the time will come' are predictive frames for vice lists; 4:1, 4:8 'that day'; 2:18 names a realized-resurrection error. Not a boundary driver beyond marking 3:1-9.
evidence.connections: Pastoral and Pauline-circle links (Hymenaeus 2:17 // 1 Tim 1:20; Alexander 4:14 // 1 Tim 1:20; 2:22-26 // 1 Tim 6:11; 1:9-10 // Titus 3:4-7 and Eph 2:8-9; 2:8 // Rom 1:3-4; 2:11 // Rom 6:8); Acts links (1:5 Lois and Eunice with Acts 16:1; 3:11 Antioch, Iconium, Lystra with Acts 13:50; 14:5, 19; 4:11 Mark with Acts 15:37-39 and Col 4:10; 4:20 Erastus and Trophimus with Acts 19:22; 20:4; 21:29; 4:10 Demas with Col 4:14/Phlm 24; 4:12 Tychicus with Eph 6:21/Col 4:7); OT: 2:19 Num 16:5; 3:8 Exod 7:11 with the Jannes/Jambres tradition (CD 5:18); 4:14 Ps 62:12/Prov 24:12; 4:17 Ps 22:21.
evidence.ecclesial_contestedness: Reception fact, not adjudicated: 3:15-17 inspiration and sufficiency of Scripture (sola scriptura vs Scripture-and-Tradition; which 'sacred writings' Timothy knew, bearing on the deuterocanon); 1:16-18 Onesiphorus (cited in Catholic/Orthodox practice of prayer for the departed, read otherwise by Protestant interpreters); 1:6 laying on of hands and 2:2 entrusting to faithful men (ordination and succession); 2:11-13 denial and faithfulness in assurance/perseverance debates; 4:8 crown in merit discussions; 3:8 extra-canonical tradition; authorship of the Pastorals disputed.

books.boundary_risk: 2:11a may attach backward or forward, moving the 2:8-13 seam; 3:1-9 and 3:10-17 form one 'but you' antithesis that a topical split severs; 1:15-18 (Asian deserters, Onesiphorus) interrupts the 1:6-14 to 2:1 charge; 2:14-26 has sub-starts (2:19 seal, 2:20-21 vessels, 2:22) prone to over-splitting; 4:1-8 charge-plus-testament must be separated from 4:9-22 personalia on a real seam.
books.uncertainty: The second line of 2:19 has no settled source (Isa 26:13, Sir 17:26 and Num 16:26 are proposed); WEB Byzantine readings at 1:11 and 4:22 not byte-verified here.

evidence.translation_difficulty: 2:13 'our great God and Savior Jesus Christ' (one referent under the article-sharing construction, or two) is christologically loaded; 3:5 loutron palingenesias 'washing of regeneration' (palingenesia only here and Matt 19:28); 2:11 sotherios pasin anthropois (grace 'that brings salvation to all' vs 'appeared to all'); 1:6 tekna pista ('believing' or 'faithful' children); 3:10 hairetikon (hapax: factious or heretic); 1:12 a hexameter from Epimenides; 2:5 oikourgous/oikourous variant; 1:5-7 presbyteroi and episkopos used of one office; 3:4-7 one long sentence; Byzantine 'mercy' at 1:4 and aphtharsian at 2:7.
evidence.literature_type_difficulty: Mandate letter with an unusually long creedal prescript (1:1-4), elder qualifications (1:5-9), polemic with a pagan poet quoted as 'a prophet of their own' (1:10-16), station-by-station household instruction (2:1-10), two hymnic/creedal soteriological summaries (2:11-14; 3:4-7, the latter possibly baptismal), civic paraenesis (3:1-2), a faithful saying (3:8), heretic procedure (3:9-11), travel notes and greetings (3:12-15).
evidence.prophecy: Low: 2:13 blessed hope and appearing; 1:12 a pagan 'prophet' quoted; epiphany language at 2:11 and 3:4 is retrospective. Not a boundary driver.
evidence.connections: Pastoral parallels (1:5-9 // 1 Tim 3:1-7; 3:9 // 1 Tim 1:4; 2:1-10 with the household codes of Col 3:18-4:1, Eph 5:22-6:9, 1 Pet 2:18-3:7; 3:1 with Rom 13:1-7 and 1 Pet 2:13-17; 3:4-7 // 2 Tim 1:9-10); 2:14 is an LXX mosaic (Ps 130:8 'redeem from all iniquity'; Exod 19:5/Deut 7:6, 14:2 'a people of his own'; Ezek 37:23); 3:5-6 Ezek 36:25-27 and Joel 2:28 (washing, outpouring); 1:15 with Luke 11:41; 1:12 Epimenides (compare Acts 17:28); Titus in 2 Cor 2:13, 7:6-16, 8:6-23 and Gal 2:1-3 but absent from Acts; 3:13 Apollos with Acts 18:24; 3:12 Tychicus with Eph 6:21/Col 4:7; Crete with Acts 27:7-13.
evidence.ecclesial_contestedness: Reception fact, not adjudicated: 3:5 baptismal regeneration (cited in Catholic, Orthodox and Lutheran baptismal teaching; read as Spirit-washing or symbol by many Reformed and Baptist interpreters); 2:13 deity of Christ (Arian and Jehovah's Witness renderings vs Nicene readings); 1:5-7 elder/bishop identity in polity (presbyterian vs episcopal); 1:6 'husband of one wife' and believing children in clergy rules; 2:3-5 women teaching women; 2:9-10 slaves in reception history; 3:10 procedure for a 'heretic' in discipline; 2:11 grace 'to all' in universal-grace debates; 3:5 'not by works' in justification; authorship disputed.

books.boundary_risk: 3:8a 'faithful is the saying' points back to 3:4-7, so a seam at 3:8 severs the saying from its formula; 2:11-14 grounds 2:1-10 with 'for' and 2:15 closes the section, so a seam at 2:11 strands the warrant; 1:10 'for' binds the polemic to the qualifications; 3:3-7 'for we ourselves were once' continues 3:1-2; the 1:1-4 prescript is a creedal unit and easily over-split.
books.uncertainty: WEB rendering of 2:13 and the Byzantine 1:4 'mercy' not byte-verified here.
